_README: Your stated priorities, encoded. Edit any number here and re-run
Weights are 0-10 RELATIVE IMPORTANCE within a position. They control how
much the model LEANS on each scoring route when projecting. They do NOT
change what a route is worth when it happens -- a goal is 6 pts for a FWD
and 4 for a MID because the rules say so, and no weight overrides that.
alpha = how much your judgement counts vs the fitted 2025-26 data.
0 = ignore me entirely, 1 = ignore the data entirely.

GKP._note: Nailed 90 mins is a HARD FILTER, not a weight -- see hard_constraints.

_note: Weights are CONDITIONAL on team strength -- this is a real model
change, not a single weight. See defender_team_split below.
DEF._set_piece_note: Lowered 7->3: only team-level set-play xG and aerial duels available as proxies. Heavy weight on a noisy input amplifies measurement error. Raise once player-level set-piece data exists.

MID._consistency_note: Redefined: was overlapping minutes_security (both mapped to start rate). Now measures RETURN FREQUENCY - share of matches with a goal or assist - not minutes. Weight 8->6 since minutes is counted separately.

_note: Your point: for weak teams DefCon > clean sheets, because clean sheets
are unlikely. For strong teams DefCon and attacking returns rank about
equally, because when a good team wins comfortably the defender is less
likely to take bonus.
Split is on team Elo. 1800 is roughly the current league median.

hard_constraints._note: Filters, not weights. Applied before optimisation.
hard_constraints.gk_rationale: You said GKs must be nailed 90 mins, no question.

_note: You said you'd gamble on a MID or FWD with exceptional data but shaky
minutes -- never on a GK, and DEF needs guaranteed minutes.
Value is the minimum start probability before the player is excluded,
and the xP multiplier required to override it.
You flagged these as very important. Applied as an xP multiplier on the
relevant component, not as a flat bonus.
Penalties boost xG; corners and free kicks boost xA and set-piece xG.
Your two profiles. Scored separately, then the model takes the higher --
a player only has to be good at ONE of these to be worth owning.
Premium forwards must justify price with frequent returns, not one big
haul. Cheap forwards are where differentials come from, so the model is
allowed to rate them highly on strong underlying data.
The big one. You are optimising RANK, not raw points. Being 'boring'
and close to template protects rank; differentials only pay when they
hit. This changes the OPTIMISER OBJECTIVE, not just weights.
objective = E[points] - lambda * ownership_risk
ownership_risk penalises NOT owning a highly-owned player far more than
it penalises owning an unowned one, because the downside is asymmetric.
captain_template_bias near 1.0 means: only captain a differential when
its xP edge is large enough to justify the rank risk.

How hard to discount players the model has little data on. A tier-D player's xP is built from a positional average, not evidence, so it should not compete on equal terms with a proven starter. selection_score is multiplied by (floor + (1-floor) * confidence). floor=1.0 disables this; lower = more sceptical.
